answer: The existing library is a suitable base for a future multi-session engine: multiple request-local cache histories, exact page permissions and versioned state are already expressible. A user/session-aware serving engine, automatic cache policy and a multi-user Qwen service have not been delivered by the cited tests.

facts.fact: One paged or ragged batch can describe several sequences with different query counts and KV histories. query_indptr groups query rows; kv_indptr groups page references or ragged KV rows; page_indices and last_page_lengths select each request's physical history. Immutable active-layout versions are bounded by a fixed schema. This is request-indexed math/layout, not user authentication or session naming.
facts.tested_scope: Ordinary E4 CPU/CUDA/Apple/Vulkan reference: two requests with 1+3 query rows, independently bounded histories, nonmonotonic/repeated physical pages, separate K/V scales, independent invocation slots, retained old results, Q1 growth and fresh comparison. This proves the listed finite batching/layout/resource cases; it does not prove a dynamic serving scheduler.

facts.fact: PagedArena owns a bounded physical arena with independent page blocks. Readers retain exact pages and initialized prefixes; repeated references share guards. A ready page can be reacquired only after other readers and actual native uses retire. Explicit copy-to-new-page plus a new layout supports branch/append without modifying an old version. Shared readonly prefix pages are representable; prefix lookup, automatic tail COW and eviction selection are caller policy.
facts.important_boundary: Dropping a session directory entry or observing cancellation does not make an in-flight page writable. Pages remain pinned through original permissions and actual Completion retirement. Arena acquisition does not silently grow the cache. Page choice/eviction is explicitly caller policy in the public header.

facts.fact: StateStore can retain resource ReadLeases and host metadata as one immutable StateVersion; StateDraft updates selected members, explicit clone_for_write creates writable copies, and StateHead publishes against an expected StateIdentity. A stale expected base returns Unavailable. Store/head methods are thread-safe, but each Draft/Writer/Ticket needs an externally synchronized owner. Separate in-flight requests need distinct admitted slots and bindings, not concurrent mutation of one Invocation.
facts.tested_scope: Published native lifetime evidence contains 3 standalone CUDA/Vulkan/Apple processes, 15 PASS journeys (not gtest cases), including successful clone publication, distinct old/new readers after teardown, cancelled/failed old controls retained through actual retirement and cold rearm, and observer-aware close. Common CPU clone/page-version tests are separate evidence, not automatically a GPU page-COW execution claim.

facts.fact: The existing producer-to-pending-page reader chain is not restricted to pure CUDA. The finite E4 chain was executed as CPU Direct/Graph, CUDA Direct/GPU Graph/CPU+GPU Graph, and Apple/Vulkan native plus CPU+GPU compositions. Owned page binding and accepted copy prefixes use the original Graph sequence/Completion. These are operation/consumer capabilities subject to native geometry, encoding and device limits, not complete model/service support on all paths.
facts.tested_scope: e4-paired-pending reference: 7 backend-scoped cases, 0 failure/skip; 9 success episodes, 18 expected-failure episodes, 54 update rounds. Two requests; each episode has six dirty-page updates, paired/independent encoders, old readers, no publication on failure and original retirement. No throughput/concurrent-client service claim.

facts.fact: The current Qwen3.5 consumer is CUDA-only and single-session: one Model owns one length/parity and 24 layer state entries. Six attention layers retain K/V; eighteen linear-attention layers retain BF16 convolution history plus F32 GDN recurrent state with parity slots. Session restore/branch/interleave must preserve all these resources and position/geometry metadata together. Swapping only KV would be incorrect. The present multi-turn schedule exercises one persistent session, not multiple users or a Qwen mixed/CPU engine.
facts.weights: Readonly resources and compiled artifacts can be shared according to their original contracts. The current Model constructor loads its own weights; creating one unchanged Model per user is not an implemented shared-weight serving design. No memory-saving claim follows from that shortcut.

engine_policy_to_supply: A host session registry mapping user/session identity to the correct StateHead/version, page ownership, positions and hybrid state; request ordering and access policy are not encoded by a batch ordinal.

A bounded page allocator/free-page ledger and admission/quota/eviction policy. Existing capacity checks and ResourceBudget provide limits, not scheduling or fairness. Retired permissions, not request cancellation alone, permit physical reuse.

Prefix identity/lookup and explicit share-or-COW policy, including partially filled tail pages and non-KV hybrid states. Existing readonly sharing and clone primitives do not implement automatic prefix matching.

A changing active-request scheduler that constructs immutable per-step batch layouts and assigns original independent execution slots. Multi-request layouts do not themselves implement continuous batching or request cancellation orchestration.

A complete model-level publication/cancellation protocol joining page updates and conv/GDN/metadata versions, preserving old results until the original native work retires. No new executor is required by this source review.
smallest_next_consumer: An engine-side bounded two-session journey could interleave requests, then join and remove requests from a shared batch while checking each against an isolated reference; retain one old result, cancel one accepted update, prove actual retirement before page reuse, and branch a shared readonly prefix with an explicit private tail. For Qwen include conv/GDN and positions in the same session version. This is a proposed next consumer, not a passed test or authorized implementation in this review.

published_evidence.scope: Finite ordinary paged E4 encoding/reading, multi-request layout and retained results across four backends; later pending-chain proof is the separate newer evidence below.
Actual finite paired/independent encoder -> copy -> pending page reader on CPU/GPU/mixed routes, including expected failures.
Native version/clone ownership, old controls, failure/cancel, observers and retirement; no model/server claim.

claim_boundaries: No multi-user server, automatic session namespace, continuous-batching policy, universal prefix cache or model-level hybrid-state integration is claimed delivered.
Public page/state handles preserve borrowing rules: Context/MemoryResource/allocator must outlive their native uses and escaped readers.
Different backends/formats/geometries retain actual qualification and reuse restrictions; a passing small multi-request case is not arbitrary request count, shape or concurrent throughput coverage.
This review ran no test, model, GPU or build and changed no product/source/test/documentation. It reuses named historical actual test evidence and reads current source.
